answer_text: Oersted saw that a compass needle near a wire swings when current is switched on, proving that electricity produces magnetism. For a straight wire the right-hand thumb rule gives the field: point the thumb along the current and the fingers curl in the direction of the circular field lines. A long solenoid produces a field like that of a bar magnet, uniform inside and with definite north and south ends, so with a soft-iron core it is used as an electromagnet. An electric motor converts electrical energy to rotation: a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a force given by Fleming's left-hand rule. A generator does the reverse. A coil is rotated in a field so the flux changes, an emf is induced (Faraday's law), and Fleming's right-hand rule gives the current direction.
